diagnosis.what_happened: Hooks were previously centralized into a global dispatcher (hook_dispatcher.py) with 66+ hook files in .agents/hooks/agents/ because earlier Antigravity versions lacked agent-scoped hook selectors.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Required complex runtime identity resolution, transcript reverse-engineering, and fast-paths to prevent developer agent interference.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: Under Antigravity 2.17+, each agent should declare its scoped hooks directly in its own folder and front matter (agent.md), co-locating definitions, contracts, and guardrails.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Atomic self-contained agent modules eliminate centralized dispatcher bottlenecks, eliminate hook pollution, and preserve developer velocity natively.

desired_behavior: Package each agent and subagent as an autonomous unit containing its definition (agent.md), contracts (contract.md), and dedicated lifecycle guard (guard.py / hooks.json) within its own dedicated folder.
generalization: Co-locate agent-specific lifecycle hooks and governance guards inside each agent's individual directory (.agents/agents/<agent>/), declaring them via frontmatter hooks: in agent.md.

evidence.observed_value: Antigravity 2.17.0 supports scoped hooks: in Markdown agent frontmatter with relative path resolution.
evidence.threshold_value: 100% native engine scoping without central Python dispatcher.
